facts.condition: Within that specialized system, discarding conditional correlation between the two auxiliary receivers while retaining each receiver's conditional marginal leaves every constraint unchanged; the converse search may therefore use separate binary-input receiver channels.

When all relevant posterior input probabilities are restricted to zero, one half, or one, feasibility and objective expressions depend on each auxiliary receiver only through its mutual-information value at the fair input distribution, producing a well-defined finite scalar optimization on realizable parameter pairs.

Under the same converse premise, the posterior-restricted optimization cannot exceed its unrestricted fair-prior counterpart, which in turn cannot exceed the corresponding full-prior receiver bound; minimizing the latter over admissible receiver pairs gives a private-message sum-rate upper bound.

Conditional on the adopted two-receiver converse theorem, setting the common-message rate to zero yields a thirty-inequality scalar system that agrees with the independently derived length-three dependency-chain formulation.

assumptions: All auxiliary alphabets and auxiliary receiver outputs are finite.
No numerical optimum, receiver-cardinality reduction, coercive estimate, or continuum-limit conclusion is assumed.
Optimization over an infeasible restricted class is interpreted in the extended-real sense, and no attainment or closure property is assumed.
The cited two-auxiliary-receiver converse theorem is used as an unproved premise; the accepted claim does not establish its source authenticity or rederive the theorem.
